title: Interleaved Canary Triage Protocol & Stakeholder Map (working)
body:
Purpose: quick operational protocol for diagnosing and triaging interleaved canaries where multiple feature variations and model routing changes are live simultaneously. Focus is on fast, repeatable decisions, clear stakeholder handoffs, and minimal blast radius.

Scope: applies to multi-arm canary experiments and staged rollouts that change routing rules, model variants, or inference pricing tiers. Not intended for full A/B analysis methodology (see experiment-statistics team doc), but to be used when there is cross-team impact and the automated safeguards either did not catch the issue or were intentionally bypassed.

High-level principles (short):
- Fast containment over perfect root cause. Get service back to stable quickly, then investigate.
- Single owner for the triage window (the steward). Whoever declared the activation becomes temporary steward unless an oncall SRE takes over.
- Always document the quick decision (why we cut traffic, what we rolled back) in the activity log channel.
- Prefer routing-level mitigations (slice quarantine, weighted-shift) before full rollback if latency/cost at risk.

Roles & contact map (working):
- Steward (activation owner): usually product PM or release owner. Primary contact: Maya Thompson (product).
- Orchestrator (console operator): person using the activation console to change slices, quotas, or routing. Primary: Ethan Wong (ops).
- Model lead: owns behavior/regressions for model variants. Primary: Sofia Martinez (applied-ml).
- SRE oncall: escalation for infra/latency/availability. Primary: Pager SRE rotation (see oncall roster).
- Support escalation: frontline CS engineer for customer-facing incidents. Primary: Oliver Chen (customer-success).

Triage phases (flow):
1) Signal detection (0-5m):
  - Inputs: automated canary alarms (latency spike, token cost delta, quality drift), user complaints, synthetic probe failures, telemetry anomaly.
  - Immediate action: steward acknowledges, posts short triage summary to #rollout-ops with activation id, start time, primary symptom.

2) Containment (5-20m):
  - If symptom is availability (5xx / high tail latency): orchestrator reduces new-traffic weight for affected slice(s) by at least 50% or quarantines slice. If multiple slices implicated, apply conservative multi-slice throttling.
  - If symptom is quality (semantic regression / hallucination): model lead suggests slicing by content-type (e.g., edge-cases), reduce exposure to the variant or switch to stable model; consider enabling human-in-loop for affected cohort.
  - If symptom is cost/regression in token consumption: apply per-route token cap and throttle high-consuming users; consider fallback to a quantized cheaper variant.
  - Record containment step and reason in the activity log.

3) Diagnosis (20-120m):
  - Gather quick artifacts: sample request logs, top-50 failure snippets, latency histograms, model kv-cache hit ratio, routing config diff.
  - Use synthetic traffic to repro in a sandboxed slice where possible (no noisy sampling).
  - If root cause intersects infra (GPU OOM, kernel mismatch), SRE owns hotfix; else model lead or product iterates.

4) Decision & Recovery (2-24h):
  - Options: resume with modified split, full rollback to pinned version, partial rollback of only specific cohorts, or keep in quarantine with mitigations.
  - Steward calls the decision after consulting all stakeholders. If disagreement and user-impacting, default to conservative rollback.
  - Document rollback/change and create follow-up ticket with tags: incident:canary, followup:evals, followup:infra if needed.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Low-severity: steward + orchestrator.
- Medium (persistent latency or quality drop affecting >1% active users): bring in model lead and SRE.
- High (customer SLA breach, data exposure, unsafe outputs): page executive oncall, CS director, legal if PII involved.

Decision heuristics cheat-sheet (quick):
- If 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 15m and trending up -> throttle slices & page SRE.
- If avg token count per request increases >40% vs baseline without clear prompt-change -> cap route + model lead review.
- If human-rated quality score drops >= 0.15 A/B uplift loss in early cohort -> reduce exposure by 75% and enable manual review.
- If model outputs hit defined safety triggers (see safety-net list) -> immediate full rollback and safety postmortem.

Stakeholder handoff templates (use in #rollout-ops):
- Short notice (first message): "ACTIVATION [id] — steward ack. symptom: [latency/quality/cost]. containment: [throttle/quarantine/rollback]. steward: [name]. orchestrator: [name]."
- Follow-up (post containment): include 3 bullets: quick metrics, sample anomalies (1-3 lines), next action.

Synthetic traffic playbook (lightweight):
- When triaging routing problems, run targeted synthetic probes against the problematic path with identical headers and prompt templating. Keep probe volume low (<=1% of normal peak) and route to sandboxed backend.
- Use golden prompts (from evals) to test quality regressions, maintain a short list per model variant.

Notes on interleaving complexity (lessons learned):
- Simultaneous small changes (weight shifts across many slices) create combinatorial noise in telemetry. Prefer single-variable changes during high-traffic windows.
- Time-of-day effects: schedule nontrivial interleaved activations to low-traffic windows with longer guardrails.
- Keep a short mapping of which UX funnels map to which slices (so triage can identify affected user cohorts faster).

Quick incident example (mini-runbook):
- 2025-02-07 morning activation: introduced routing rule for low-latency variant + price-tier fallback. 10m after activation, tail latency 95p rose from 1.1s -> 2.4s.
- Steward posted to #rollout-ops, orchestrator quarantined the low-latency variant slice, SRE found intermittent kernel mismatch on a subset of GPU nodes. Model lead ran golden prompts, no quality change. Decision: keep low-latency variant quarantined, route traffic back to baseline for 2h, escalate infra fix.

Open questions (to resolve):
- Should we add an automated pre-commit checklist that prevents >N simultaneous slice changes in a single activation? (pro: reduces noise; con: slows experiments)
- Can we instrument a per-activation unique id that flows through logs + traces to make slicing gaps trivial to filter? (high priority)
- What are precise SLA thresholds that auto-trigger paging for canaries? Current SRE thresholds assume production, not canary noise — need joint definition.

Immediate action items (TODOs):

- [Ethan] prototype a lightweight activation-id header propagation in routing layer (due 2025-02-28).
- [Sofia] assemble golden-prompt list per model variant (first pass 2025-03-07).
- [All] trial a runbook rehearsal for interleaved-canary triage during next ops-day (schedule: 2025-03-14).
